The archive behaviour is verified end-to-end: archiving moves a bookmark out of **All** (4 → 3) into **Archive**, the Archived badge shows, and Restore brings it back (All returns to 4). Refresh **http://maker:4001** and try it yourself.

You now have a third tab, **Archive**:

> **1.** In the **All** view, pick a bookmark you want out of the way — say "The Practical Test Pyramid" — and click **Archive**. It disappears from All immediately (decluttering your main list), and the **Archive** tab count ticks up.
> **2.** Click the **Archive** tab. There's your archived bookmark, kept safe with an **Archived** badge — nothing was deleted.
> **3.** On that card, click **Restore to library**. It returns to your **All** view.

Two decisions I made that I'd like your reaction to:

- **Archiving *moves* the bookmark** out of All (and out of Read Later), unlike the read-later marker which left it in place. Archived links live only under the Archive tab until you restore them. Does that "set completely aside, but retained" behaviour match what you meant by archiving?
- **In the Archive view I pared the card's actions down** to just *Restore to library* — no editing or tagging while it's archived. Is that the right call, or would you still want to manage a bookmark while it's archived?

Give archiving a try and tell me whether it declutters your main view the way you intended.
